newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - March 14.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - March 14.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:
(2x4 Std&Btr) WEEKLY MIDWEEK PREV WK YR AGO

COMMENT - An early surge in sales failed to snap the market out of its lethargy and most prices ended the week flat or lower, Random Lengths said. Activity improved briefly on Tuesday when secondaries covered short positions at the same time buyers were polishing off purchases before leaving for a WWPA meeting.

Tuesday's futures-led round of short-covering was brief and trading slowed again Wednesday. With many industry decision makers out of their offices attending the Western Wood Products Association gathering in San Francisco, the market wasn't able to get back on track Thursday. So the Framing Lumber Index ended up falling $3 but remained in the year's narrow range.

Buyers appreaed unconcerned about supplies as the end of the quota year approached for Canadian producers. Most customers said they were finding enough Canadian lumber from one source or another, and many seemed more concerned about a surge of unsold wood hitting the market after the April 1 new quota year starts.

Lingering winter weather kept already-sold stock bottled up in dealers' yards, giving bulls an argument for a pickup as soon as jobsites clear, Random Lengths said. Weather slowed output at some westside Southern Pine mills, as it has for the last month.

Many buyers readily admitted that there was a risk to keeping a tight lid on inventories with Spring just around the corner. But with prices well above year-ago levels, most were not inclined to load up stocks. Many secondaries were equally cautious and some openly bearish, citing forecasts that housing starts will ease off this year. Upward momentum eased in some board prices but 12-inch pine and spruce supply remained tight.
Western red cedar prices were stable for a third week.
Canadian lumber exports as of March 6 were at 77.2 percent of fee-free quarterly quota and 95.6 pct of annual quota. (Chicago newsdesk 312 408 8720)
